items.statement: HTLS product carries double-digit margins; INR 200 cr+ HTLS order book to aid margin improvement; HTLS to help exceed FY25 margins more comfortably
items.quote: HTLS by itself could give us double-digit margins. But then HTLS order book is roughly INR200 crores as of now.

items.statement: Structural drivers strong: grid strengthening, renewables, railways/metro, data centers; multiyear programs reflected in inquiries and order flow

items.statement: HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type up to 765 kV), EHV cables up to 220 kV, e-beam cables, rubber cables identified as margin-accretive growth segments; Narmadapuram to house these
items.quote: Narmadapuram is what allows us to move up the value chain with EHV cables up to 220 kV, specialized conductors, including HTLS and e-beam cables.

items.statement: Data center approvals established with leading developers representing substantial share of hyperscale/colocation capex; approvals with others progressing
items.quote: We have established approvals with leading data center developers and the customers where we are approved, represent a substantial share of the hyperscale and colocation capex being planned in the country.

items.statement: U.S. tariff framework stabilized post Supreme Court ruling; Indian cables at par with Asian/European competitors; U.S. distributors regaining confidence
items.quote: Today, Indian cables are at par with the competing exporting countries in Asia and Europe. One expects that the tariff framework in the U.S. now rests on a more stable footing than sudden changes that we lived through last year.

items.statement: Net working capital 108 days (vs 101 days end FY26) due to accelerated supplier payments post equity raise; receivables improved 79 to 66 days; target 90-100 days in H2 FY27

items.statement: Net worth INR 920 cr; debt-equity 0.14x; long-term loans to be tied up for Narmadapuram; debt-equity expected ~0.3x post commissioning, not exceeding 0.6-0.7x
items.quote: Our net worth stood at INR 920 crores as of 30th September '26, and our debt-equity ratio remains comfortable at 0.14x.

items.statement: National Electricity Plan projects INR 5 lakh cr investment in EHV transmission lines 2027-2032; management estimates HTLS reconductoring market ~INR 50,000 cr over next 5 years
items.quote: As per our internal assessment of the tenders announced by multiple utilities, state governments and central government authorities, the management projects the market size for reconductoring projects of HTLS to be approximately INR 50,000 crores in the next 5 years.

items.statement: No ambition to enter high-advertising B2C house wire segment (~INR 100 cr of ~INR 2,000 cr revenue); B2B strength from 70-year footprint and approvals; new Narmadapuram products face less competition
items.quote: We do not have any ambitions to jump into that extra competitive, high advertising cost and high distribution cost segment. We have a very limited exposure to B2C business, and that is quite steady.

items.statement: U.S. IEEPA tariffs struck down by Supreme Court in Feb 2026; tariff framework now stable; customers carry tariff changes to their account
items.quote: As you know, the IEEPA tariffs was shut down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. Today, Indian cables are at par with the competing exporting countries in Asia and Europe.

items.statement: Metal booking discipline: firm-price orders booked next working day; no firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months delivery; aluminum >75% of metal value consumption; aluminum softened in quarter
items.quote: The day we receive a firm-price order, the next working day we book the metal, and mostly, we do not accept firm-price orders beyond 3 to 4 months delivery.

items.statement: Metal price volatility and global trade environment remain key challenges; HTLS execution involves EPC/installation with potentially longer deliveries; 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years
items.quote: The wires and cable industry continued to navigate two familiar challenges this quarter- metal price volatility and the global trade environment that is still settling down.

items.statement: Consolidated FY27 capex increased to about INR150 crores across fasteners, DC contactors and MCUs

items.quote: Our -- on our stand-alone fasteners business, the initial capex plan was INR80 crores, which has been ramped up to maybe close to more like INR130 crores this year -- sorry, INR120 crores this year.

items.quote: While industry sales grew by approximately 18% in Q2 FY27, our stand-alone revenue increased by around 32% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: CV segment strong traction, particularly high volumes from a marquee customer driving outperformance

items.quote: Our H1 EBITDA increased by 17% year-on-year to INR58.7 crores, whereas for Q2 FY27, EBITDA increased to INR27.7 crores, reflecting a growth of around 8% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure from input cost inflation; low-cost inventory exhausted in Q1; pass-through with time lag
items.quote: As discussed on our previous earnings calls, we exhausted most of our earlier low-cost inventory in Q1. At the same time, commodity and non-commodity input costs have increased significantly amid the ongoing West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve over coming quarters as higher costs progressively recovered, subject to input prices
items.quote: As the higher costs are progressively recovered, we expect margins to improve over the coming quarters, subject to input price movements and broader operating environment.

items.statement: Fastener EBITDA margin historically 15-16%; hope to maintain but exceptional inflation may cause marginal pressure this year
items.quote: On the fasteners business, we've been hovering between 15% and 16% EBITDA. Like I said a little while ago, we hope to maintain that. But this year is an exceptional year.

items.statement: Target to reach 15% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 on quarterly basis
items.quote: We are hoping that. That's correct.

items.statement: Input costs up dramatically: some commodities up 300%, others 30-50%; tungsten carbide up over 300% in 12 months
items.quote: We have seen where input costs have gone up by some commodities as much as 300%, some by 30%, 40%, 50%. So the inflationary impact has been substantial.

items.statement: Price pass-through negotiations ongoing with OEMs; some agreed, some under negotiation, some retrospective; expect substantial compensation in H2
items.quote: We are negotiating with our customers for price increases, not only on account of steel, which is a normal practice running for years, but this year exceptional item is inflation and cost increases.

items.statement: Price recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 with retrospective effect
items.quote: Correct. And some of those price increases will have a retrospective effect as well.

items.statement: SEM revenue INR23 crores in Q2, INR37 crores H1; 80% QoQ growth driven by higher-value CV/LCV applications
items.quote: Revenue from this business stood at approximately INR23 crores in Q2 FY27, taking H1FY27 revenue to around INR37 crores.

items.statement: SEM targeting INR150 crores annual revenue for breakeven; expect to outperform in FY28
items.quote: Once we reach a revenue of INR150 crores plus, we'll probably achieve breakeven point at that time.

items.quote: The production lines for onboard chargers and multifunction units scheduled for commissioning in Q2 has been commissioned as planned.

items.statement: SEM has 42 active programs, 23 business contracts; 5 new contracts entering production by year-end

items.quote: Commercial supplies, which were scheduled to begin in Q2 FY27, have now commenced.

items.quote: Despite that acquisition of that competitor by an Italian company, we don't feel any pressure coming to us on account of that. There is no pricing pressure. There is no volume pressure.

items.statement: 9 MW captive solar plant (5.5 MW Rajasthan, 3.5 MW Gujarat) targeting Q4 FY27 commissioning; to meet ~40% power needs
items.quote: We are building 9 MW of captive solar capacity across two plants – 5.5 MW in Rajasthan and 3.5 MW in Gujarat. The total investment is about ₹29 crores and we are targeting commissioning in the fourth quarter of this financial year. Once running, solar should meet about 40% of our power needs.

items.statement: Captive talc mine in Andhra Pradesh and quartz/feldspar mine in Rajasthan to start production from December 2026
items.quote: Our new talc mine in Andhra Pradesh and our quartz and feldspar mine in Rajasthan are expected to begin production from December 2026.

items.statement: Solar project estimated to deliver ~₹8 crore annual EBITDA benefit (~80 bps margin) from FY29 at grid tariff ₹3.45-3.5/kWh net of O&M
items.quote: We reduce the tariff to around ₹3.45–3.5 [as heard]. That is how the economics will work, and based on that we expect a benefit of around ₹8 crores per year from FY29

Gas has risen from ₹69 to ₹122 per kg, around 77%, an impact of ₹0.62 crores. Freight per metric tonne has gone from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346, an 11% rise, an impact of around ₹2.92 crores.

items.quote: Functional additives – more than 250 specialised grades that we already carry in our portfolio – contribute about one quarter of our revenue. items.quote: The specialty products have already started to contribute to margins. You have to look at 20 Microns on a consolidated basis – if you look at 20 Microns Nano as an individual company, it has grown in double digits this quarter and its profitability has also increased.

items.statement: Bid placed in Government of India PLI scheme for rare-earth permanent magnets (REPM); awaiting results in next couple of months
items.quote: 20 Microns has placed its bid in the PLI scheme launched by the Government of India for rare-earth permanent magnets (REPM), in which 20 bidders participated. items.statement: EBITDA margins consistently between 12-14% for over a decade despite pandemic, supply-chain disruptions and energy/freight cost swings
items.quote: Through a pandemic, supply-chain disruptions and sharp swings in energy and freight costs, our EBITDA margins have stayed between 12% and 14% year after year for over a decade.

items.statement: Q3/Q4 margins hard to predict due to supply-chain disruptions, wars and upcoming midterm elections; wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: For Q3 and Q4, as I mentioned, it is very hard to predict – not only for us but for all industries – given the ongoing supply-chain disruptions, the wars and the upcoming midterm elections. We don't know what's ahead, so it's a wait-and-watch situation; we hope things don't get worse.

items.statement: Customer relationships span 10-25 years; new grades take 3-10 years from brief to commercial supply; leading FMCG company moving to commercial supply after nearly 10 years of trials
items.quote: A new grade typically takes anywhere from three to ten years to move from the first brief to commercial supply. A leading FMCG company is only now moving into commercial supply after nearly ten years of trials with us. items.statement: Inventory normalising and cash flow catching up with profits expected over coming months as mines start December 2026 and solar commissions Q4 FY27
items.quote: Several of the actions I described should start to show in the numbers over the coming months: inventory normalising and cash flow catching up with profits. With both mines starting production from December and the solar plants commissioning in Q4, the full-year benefit will come from FY28.

items.statement: Employee costs increased in Q2 FY27 as teams strengthened in preparation for planned capacity expansion
items.quote: The quarter's operating performance was impacted by higher power and fuel costs, export freight expenses and some increase in employee costs as we strengthen our teams in preparation for our planned capacity.

items.statement: Power demand grew 11.1% YoY in Q2 FY27, with September up 11.3% and October month-to-date up 21.2%; management sees structural drivers supporting 5-6% long-term CAGR.
items.quote: Power demand in Q2 FY27 grew about 11.1% year -on-year, building on 8.3% growth in Q1. September alone grew about 11.3%, with peak demand touching 270 GW in Q2FY27. The momentum strengthened further into October, with month-to-date demand growth of 21.2%.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY27 is around ₹20,000 crore to support the 3 GW commissioning target and 1 GWh of energy storage projects.
items.quote: The pipeline is substantially de-risked, and we are confident of achieving our 3 GW commissioning target for FY27, supported by planned capex of around ₹20,000 crore. Further, on our energy storage pursuits, we expect to commission about 1 GWh of projects in FY27.

items.statement: Installed capacity exceeded 15.1 GW with renewables at ~61%; 1.4 GW organic renewable capacity commissioned since April (513 MW in Q2), plus 300 MW Maruti thermal acquisition.
items.quote: Since April, we have commissioned 1.4 GW of organic renewable capacity as compared to last full year’s approximately 1.2 GW. This is also nearly half of our FY27 target of 3 GW. In Q2, we added 513 MW, comprising 301 MW of solar and 212 MW of hybrid capacity. items.statement: Utkal thermal plant EBITDA more than tripled YoY to ₹368 crore in Q2 FY27, driven by better plant performance and PPA realisations well above DAM prices.
items.quote: Utkal had an exceptional quarter, now that it operates under long -term PPAs. Plant EBITDA more than tripled year -on-year to ₹368 crore in Q2 FY27, and grew over 60% YoY in H1 FY27. This was driven by significantly better plant performance and by PPA realisations well above the DAM prices at which the plant's power was sold a year ago.

items.statement: Merchant realisation averaged ₹6.9/kWh in Q2 FY27, ~20% above DAM average of ₹5.7/kWh; Q3 fully booked at similar or better pricing.
items.quote: Day-Ahead Market prices averaged ₹5.7 per unit in Q2 FY27. Our merchant realisation, however, stood around ₹6.9 per unit which was around 20% higher than the DAM average, driven by the strategic bilateral contracts we have entered into.

items.statement: API4 imported coal prices averaged ~US$115/t in Q2 FY27, up 28% YoY; shift to domestic coal and job-work arrangements insulated fuel costs.
items.quote: API4 benchmark coal prices averaged close to US$115 per tonne in Q2 FY27, up around 28% year-on-year from US$90 per tonne. Despite this increase, our transition to domestic coal and the implementation of job -work arrangements at imported -coal plants, which shield us from fuel-price volatility, have enabled us to effectively mitigate the impact and maintain cost competitiveness.

items.statement: Net Debt/TTM EBITDA (ex-CWIP) improved to 4.94x from 5.2x in FY26; cash & equivalents ~₹15,700 crore; debt cost fell 51 bps YoY to 8.28%; 25% of term debt fixed for 5-6 years, 90% of floating linked to MCLR.
items.quote: Excluding debt tied to capital work-in-progress, our Net Debt to TTM EBITDA stands at about 4.94 times, down from about 5.2 times in FY26. We hold cash and cash equivalents of about ₹15,700 crore, and our cash return on net worth, adjusted for our JSW Steel shareholding, stands at about 15%.

items.statement: ₹10,150 crore capital unlocked in calendar year via fundraising and JSW Steel share sale; ICRA and India Ratings affirmed AA/Stable rating.
items.quote: ICRA and India Ratings have affirmed JSW Energy's long-term credit rating at AA with a Stable outlook. This recognises our larger and more diversified operating base, our high share of contracted capacity, and the d eleveraging we delivered through the ₹10,150 crore capital unlocking in this calendar year

items.statement: Acquired Maruti Clean Coal & Power in August at EV ₹1,410 crore; EBITDA/PAT accretive from day one, generated ₹45 crore EBITDA in 55 days; 195 MW under long-term PPA, 64 MW merchant.
items.quote: We completed the acquisition of Maruti Clean Coal & Power in August at an enterprise value of ₹1,410 crore. It is EBITDA and PAT accretive from day one and lowers our net leverage. About 195 MW (net) is tied up under a long-term PPA with Rajasthan discoms with around 14 years of residual life, while about 64 MW gives us merchant exposure at a time of strong prices.

items.statement: States awarded ~17 GW long-term thermal at ₹5.4-6.3/kWh in FY26; further 18 GW thermal tenders under bidding; renewables and thermal seen as complementary for firm power.
items.quote: States awarded around 17 GW of long-term thermal capacity at tariffs of about ₹5.4 to ₹6.3 per unit in FY26, and a further 18 GW of thermal tenders are currently under bidding. To us, the conclusion is simple. Renewables and thermal are not competing; they are complementary. Renewables deliver the cheapest energy, while thermal and storage keep the lights on through the evening peak.

items.quote: It will be about INR150 crores for the existing plant. And for the steel plant, as I said, we are still considering the final figures that will be investing.

items.quote: In number of days, it has increased by 4 to 5 days only because of some sales to customers who are having a high credit period.

items.quote: We are now coming around with a conclusion, we are diluting a bit more than required. And therefore, we may look at a 1:1 debt equity.

items.quote: The other thing we are examining, of course, the decision will be taken by the Board, is also to look at examini ng, suspending the dividend for 3 -4 years.

items.quote: So, with the combination of Kocks Block and reheating furnace, we have been able to increase our capacity to 300,000 tons. And we can actually increase this capacity even beyond this.

items.quote: It is almost in the same ratio as was there in the last year. So, 6% to 7% is direct and another 6% to 7% is indirect through ASC.

items.statement: Industry added ~30,000 5G BTS in Q2, total installed base ~593,000; focus shifting to densification
items.quote: With the industry adding approximately 30,000 5G BTS s during the second quarter, taking the total installed base to around 593,000.

items.statement: Total data volume up 30% YoY in Q1; 5G usage up 79% YoY, now 44% of total consumption
items.quote: In Q1, total data volume increased by 30% year -on-year, supported by an 18% rise in average monthly usage per subscriber. items.statement: Added ~2,900 macro towers and 7,900 co-locations in Q2; tower base ~270,500, co-location base ~440,200

items.statement: Tenancy ratio improved from 1.62 to 1.63 driven by sharing of existing towers
items.quote: Our industry -leading tenancy ratio has also improved from 1.62 to 1.63, driven by substantial rollout through sharing of our existing towers.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA grew 2.5% QoQ to INR46.3bn; EBITDA margin improved 80bps QoQ to 54.4%
items.quote: Reported EBITDA increased by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and stands at INR46.3 billion for the quarter. Our EBITDA margin also improved by 80 basis points quarter-on-quarter and stands at 54.4% for the quarter.

items.statement: Energy margin improved to -3.6% in Q2 from -4.6% in Q1 and -4.8% YoY; diesel consumption down 11% YoY
items.quote: Our energy margin was negative 3.6% in Q2 compared to negative of 4.6% in Q1 and negative 4.8% in the corresponding quarter of last year, reflecting a significant improvement during the reported quarter. Our structured energy efficiency measures are yielding positive results, and diesel consumption is further reduced by 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Growth capex increase reflected in CWIP rising ~INR250 cr QoQ due to healthy order book; capex includes towers, tenancies, 5G upgrades, solar

items.quote: The way I look at the customer segment that we operate in, is primarily very different in ATS from what the larger NBFCs or HFCs look at. Hence, that clear segmental difference, fundamentally for me, as we progress ahead, does not put competitive pressure from these entities to my target audience.

items.statement: PLR not changed after repo hike; ALCO reviews monthly; incremental lending rates support yield on fresh disbursements
items.quote: No, not currently. We are examining it, and as and when we feel the need of a PLR change, we will make it happen.

items.statement: Liquidity ample: cash/CC limits ₹19.6 bn + unavailed sanctions ₹3 bn as of Sep 2026
items.quote: As of 30th Sep 2026, we maintained ample liquidity, including cash and cash equivalents and un -availed CC limits of Rs. 19.6 billion and documented un-availed sanctions of Rs. 3 billion.

items.statement: Q2FY27 borrowings ₹16.79 bn at 7.66%; total outstanding ₹216 bn; 30% repo-linked, rest MCLR/fixed; ALM positive
items.quote: We continued to borrow judiciously, raising around Rs. 16.79 bn at competitive rate at 7.66% for Q2FY27. As of 30th Sep 2026, total outstanding borrowings stood at Rs. 216 billion.

items.statement: 1+ DPD 3.81% (-18 bps YoY); Gross Stage 3 1.11% (-13 bps YoY); Net Stage 3 0.70% (-16 bps YoY); credit cost 24 bps H1FY27
items.quote: Our 1+ DPD improved by 18 bps YoY to 3.81% in Q2 FY27, remaining comfortably below 5%. Gross Stage 3 improved by 13 bps YoY to 1.11%, while Net Stage 3 improved by 16 bps YoY to 0.70%.

items.statement: Headcount down ~150 due to right-sizing and churn; not cutting people; investing in team; ESOP rolled out to ~200 employees
items.quote: We are not cutting down on people. We are making sure that every resource deployed is rightfully produced for the organization.

items.statement: Incentive policy revamped: starts from first disbursement, graded slabs, encourages direct sourcing within 40-50 km catchment
items.quote: The incentive structure starts from the first disbursement. Obviously, it has gradations and slabs as we move upwards.

items.statement: ROA 3.28% Q2FY27 (+9 bps QoQ); ROE 13.63% (+28 bps QoQ); CRAR 43.77%
items.quote: Our RoA expanded of 9 bps QoQ to 3.28% and RoE improved of 28 bps QoQ to 13.63% in Q2FY27.

items.statement: No asset quality hiccups expected from drought; minimal exposure to pure agri-income; Maharashtra concentration low
items.quote: No, I do not see Aavas having any hiccups on asset quality at all. On the drought situation, especially the point that you mentioned on Maharashtra, we are largely centric around Pune and some of the Marathwada districts like Latur, etc. Our concentration i s very minimal

items.statement: Insurance regulation from Apr 2027 may hit ~4% of PBT; confident to offset via higher attachment rates and risk-adjusted fee/yield levers
items.quote: Roughly about 50% of what one stands to lose mathematically because of the regulation coming in from 1st of April next year, we are very confident of pulling that through by making sure that our attachment percentages come in line with what competition is.

items.statement: Technology (SFDC, BRE, rule engines) driving productivity, pricing granularity, top-up loan automation, supervisor efficiency
items.quote: Today, we are running business rule engines which give out ranges for a transaction based on three or four facets. It is not a singular combination.

items.statement: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM was Rs. 4.02 lakh crores in Q2 FY27, up from Rs. 3.93 lakh crores in Q1 FY27, with market share of 4.61%
items.quote: Our mutual fund quarterly average AUM for quarter two of FY '27 stood at Rs. 4.02 lakh crores, compared with Rs. 3.93 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, representing a market share of 4.61%.

items.statement: Total group AUM stood at Rs. 16.28 lakh crores as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: Our total group AUM stood at Rs. 16.28 lakh crores as of September 30th, 2026.

items.statement: SIP AUM was Rs. 45,572 crores as of September 30, 2026, broadly stable vs Rs. 45,595 crores in June 2026
items.quote: Our SIP AUM stood at Rs. 45,572 crores as of September 30, 2026, broadly stable as compared with Rs. 45,595 crores in June of '26.

items.statement: Gross SIP inflows were Rs. 2,583 crores in Q2 FY27 and Rs. 5,085 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: The gross SIP inflows were Rs. 2,583 crores during this quarter and Rs. 5,085 crores during the half year of FY '27.

items.statement: Registered 5.96 lakh new SIPs in Q2 FY27, 87% sourced through digital channels
items.quote: Furthermore, we registered 5.96 lakh new SIPs during quarter two of FY '27, of which 87% were sourced through digital channels.

items.statement: Live folio base stood at 1.47 crores in Q2 FY27, added 3.6 lakh new investors in Q2 and 6.12 lakh in H1 FY27
items.quote: In quarter two of FY '27, our live folio base stood at 1.47 crores, and we added 3.6 lakh new investors as identified by their PAN. During the half year, w e added 6.12 lakh

items.statement: UTI Mutual Fund's share of industry's new SIP registration by volume was 4.08% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: UTI Mutual Fund's share of industry's new SIP registration by volume stood at 4.08% in quarter two.

items.statement: Net sales in Q2 FY27 were close to Rs. 5,720 crores; average AUM growth was around Rs. 10,000 crores
items.quote: It's close to around Rs. 10,000 crores of average AUM growth rate, and almost around Rs. 5,720 crores is from net sales.

items.statement: UTI Pension Fund AUM grew 10.97% YoY to Rs. 4.32 lakh crores as of September 30, 2026, managing 24.01% of NPS industry AUM
items.quote: UTI Pension Fund has recorded a year-on-year growth of approximately 10.97% in its AUM, reaching approximately Rs. 4.32 lakh crores as on 30th September 2026, as compared to Rs. 3.89 lakh crores as on 30th September 2025. It currently manages approximately 24.01% of the NPS industry's AUM.

items.statement: UTI International AUM was USD 1.67 billion (approx Rs. 16,063 crores) as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: UTI International, which represents our international business, has an AUM of US D1.67 billion, which is approximately Rs. 16,063 crores as on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: UTI Alternatives AUM grew 52% YoY to Rs. 4,045 crores as of September 2026
items.quote: UTI Alternatives' AUM has grown to approximately Rs. 4,045 crores, up 52% from Rs. 2,669 crores as on September of 2025.

items.statement: UTI SDOF IV crossed Rs. 1,000 crores milestone, AUM at Rs. 1,131 crores, fund size planned at Rs. 1,500 crores with greenshoe of Rs. 500 crores
items.quote: UTI SDOF IV has crossed the Rs. 1,000 crores milestone. Launched in quarter three of FY26 as the fourth fund in our SDOF series, the fund is planned as a Rs. 1,500 crores with a greenshoe option of Rs. 500 crores. It already has reached an AUM of Rs. 1,131 crores and is currently in raising and investing stage.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance maintained at Rs. 95 crores per quarter standalone and Rs. 130 crores per quarter consolidated for full financial year
items.value: 95 crores per quarter standalone, 130 crores per quarter consolidated
items.quote: As far as our overall guidance number for the employee cost is, that we are maintaining that for the standalone, it is close to around Rs. 95 crores per quarter, and for the consolidated, it is close to around Rs. 130 crores per quarter. We are maintaining that guidance number for the full financial year as well.

items.statement: Board policy to distribute 90-95% of profit as dividend; no plans for special dividend or incremental cash distribution
items.quote: So as of now, the board-level decision is that most of whatever the profit that we are generating, we will be distributing closer to 90 - 95% of that profit will be distributed as dividend. That dividend aggressive policy that we have continued over the last three to four years, and that should continue.

items.statement: Will launch UTI Classif Hybrid Long Short Fund in Q3 FY27 under SIF initiative
items.quote: We have received SEBI approval for our Specialised Investment Fund - SIF initiative and will be launching the UTI Classif Hybrid Long Short Fund in quarter three of FY27.

items.statement: UTI International to launch two new funds by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are launching a few products by the end of quarter three and quarter four. Hopefully, that should provide some traction of AUM and revenue growth in UTI International. But definitely, you will hear, either by the end of quarter three or quarter four, there are two new fund launches on the UTI International side.

items.statement: Consolidated core revenue from sale of services was Rs. 398 crores in Q2 FY27, up 2% YoY and 5% QoQ; core PAT was Rs. 131 crores, up 22% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the core income, i.e. the sale of service amounted to Rs. 398 crores, up by 2% Y-o-Y and 5% Q-o-Q. The core profit after tax for the quarter is Rs. 131 crores, up by 22% Y-o-Y and 2% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 core revenue Rs. 777 crores, up 1% YoY; core PAT Rs. 263 crores, up 15% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the core income amounted to Rs. 777 crores, up by 1% Y-o-Y. The core profit after tax for H1 FY27 is Rs. 263 crores, up by 15% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Segment yields: equity/hybrid ~73-74 bps, ETF/index ~8 bps, cash/arbitrage ~11 bps, fixed income ~20-21 bps
items.value: 73-74 bps equity, 8 bps ETF, 11 bps cash, 20-21 bps fixed income
items.quote: Yes. So, equity is roughly at around 73 -74 basis points, equity and hybrid fund. ETF and index fund will be around 8 basis points, cash and arbitrage 11, and fixed income fund is around 20-21 basis points.

items.statement: Weighted average yield flat at ~31 bps; marginal repricing impact from SEBI TER to BER changes passed to intermediaries
items.quote: I don't see any sequential increase in the yield number. The yield numbers are more or less, at a weighted average level, flat at around 31 basis points. Marginal could be there because of the repricing part.

items.statement: Equity-oriented schemes attracted Rs. 92,333 crores in Q2 FY27 industry-wide; monthly SIP contribution hit record Rs. 32,490 crores in September 2026
items.quote: Equity-oriented schemes attracted Rs. 92,333 crores in quarter two of FY '27, taking the first half FY '27 inflows to Rs. 1.83 lakh crores. In September '26, the equity inflows stood at Rs. 38,307 crores, while the monthly SIP contribution reached a record Rs. 32,490 crores.

items.statement: Small and mid-cap funds accounted for 44% of September equity inflows; flexi-cap, multi-cap, large & mid-cap, large-cap accounted for 41%
items.quote: Small and mid -cap funds accounted for 44% of September's equity inflows, while flexi -cap, multi -cap, large and mid -cap, and large -cap funds accounted another 41%.

items.statement: Equity-oriented assets 72% of average mutual fund AUM in Q2 FY27 vs ~70% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Equity-oriented assets across active and passive strategies accounted for 72% of our average mutual fund AUM, compared with approximately 70% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Launched UTI Balanced Hybrid Fund and four passive products linked to Nifty 500 and BSE India Sector Leaders indices in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During quarter two of FY27, we launched the UTI Balanced Hybrid Fund and four passive products linked to the Nifty 500 and BSE India Sector Leaders indices.

items.statement: SIP book concentration: Flexi-Cap 20.3%, sectoral/thematic 16%, Mid-Cap 15%, Large & Mid-Cap 12.7% of equity SIP inflows
items.quote: Flexi-Cap remains one of the largest, you know, contributor to the SIP book. So, nearly 20% of our inflows are coming still in Flexi-Cap, and that has remained broadly at around the same level last year from last year also. Last year it was about 19.3%, now it is about 20.3%. So, apart from that, we have funds like the sectoral and thematic funds which are contributing 16%, the Mid-Cap also contri

items.statement: Redemptions in equity coming from banks, national distributors, and to smaller extent MFDs and direct channel
items.quote: From a c hannel-wise perspective, we are seeing, you know, on the equity side redemptions are coming from banks as well as from the national distributors. There are some redemptions which are also seen from the MFDs, but banks, you know, and national distributors, we are seeing a higher amount of redemption on the equity side

items.statement: Fintech partners facilitated ~1 lakh transactions in Q2 FY27, contributed 67% of new investor acquisitions
items.quote: Our fintech partners facilitated approximate ly 1 lakh transactions during the quarter two of FY27 and these partners have contributed 67% of the new investor acquisitions.

items.statement: SIP closure rate ~70% vs industry ~80%, indicating better stickiness
items.quote: And even if you look at our closure rate of SIPs in the last quarter, while industry was trending at around 80%, our SIP closure book was around 70%. So, we are better off than industry in terms of SIP closure.

items.statement: Process optimisation generated ~Rs. 4.22 crores savings; automation reducing manual intervention
items.quote: Process optimisation generated approximately Rs. 4.22 crores in savings, while automation is reducing manual intervention.

items.statement: Delivered 10,690 training hours to sales team up to September 2026; strengthening performance management and critical talent retention
items.quote: We continue to invest in the organisational capability, with 10,690 training hours delivered to the sales team up to September of '26, while strengthening performance management and identifying critical talent for development and retention.

items.statement: Industry quarterly average AUM rose to Rs. 87.2 lakh crores in Q2 FY27 from Rs. 83.1 lakh crores in Q1 FY27; ETFs net inflows Rs. 15,501 crores in September 2026
items.quote: Industry quarterly average AUM rose to Rs. 87.2 lakh crores from Rs. 83.1 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, with ETFs recording net inflows of Rs. 15,501 crores in September '26.

items.statement: Industry SIP AUM at Rs. 17.86 lakh crores as of September 2026
items.quote: the SIP AUM being at Rs. 17.86 lakh crores for industry.

items.statement: Flexi-Cap fund remains a challenge with large outflows, though performance improved to first quartile in last three months
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, Flexi-Cap remains still the challenge for us. While we have seen some inflows in Flexi-Cap, there have been large outflows also in the fund, and that remains a fund which we are focusing on. However, if you look at the last three months' performance, we are seeing that the fund performance has shown significant improvement, and now the Flexi-Cap fund is in the first quarti

items.statement: Management maintains full-year EBITDA guidance of INR750-800 crore and expects to be closer to the upper end given strong H1 performance.
items.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance. In fact, we think we should given the strong performance in the first half of the year, we should hopefully be closer to the upper end of the guidance we have given for the year.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals portfolio targeted to grow at 20-25% year-on-year on a multi-year CAGR basis.
items.quote: But at an overall level, our aspiration is to continue to grow our specialty chemical portfolio at 20% to 25% year on year on a multi-year CAGR basis.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance maintained at INR400-500 crore, with Gajraula multipurpose plant commissioning in next few months.
items.quote: We will be investing at least INR400 crore to INR500 crore every year as we announced a couple of years back in our investor presentation also.

items.statement: CDMO pipeline peak potential near INR2,000 crore including large contract; ex-large contract peak potential INR1,500 crore+ with one-third expected this fiscal year.
items.quote: On the back of some of the incremental opportunities that we have secured, that full potential along with the big contract is close to INR2,000 crore, but even if I keep the big contract aside, we still have a big pipeline which I mentioned in my opening remarks also, with the peak potential of almost INR1,500 crore plus and at least one third of that we will we will clock in in in this year, in t

items.statement: Signed agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone Technologies for INR189 crore; shareholders agreement to be concluded soon.
items.quote: I am delighted to share that we have recently signed an agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone with an investment of INR189 crore.

items.statement: European competitor plant closures in acetic anhydride expected to strengthen demand and pricing from early next calendar year, viewed as multi-year opportunity.
items.quote: Regarding your question on the plant closure in Europe, it is a very recent development and things are still playing out on the ground. So, we expect some uplift starting to happen only from early part of next calendar year.

items.statement: Investments made over last 3-3.5 years expected to reach average 70%+ utilization by end of FY27, driving need for new multipurpose plants.
items.quote: Whatever investments we made in the last three, three and a half years, a lot of them will start reaching average 70% plus utilization levels by end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Consumer segment (personal care) grew to 7% of portfolio driven by vitamin B3 personal grade ramp-up and CDMO opportunities; targeting double digits within few quarters.
items.quote: I think one of the big reasons is as I think I have communicated in the past, we have been focusing in a big way on the personal care segment and while we already have vitamin B3 personal grade which has ramped up very quickly in recent months, we also have a few other products and a CDMO kind of opportunities where we have started to serve the customers.

items.statement: Vitamin B3 pricing softened in last few weeks, may linger into Q3; pyridine base pricing under pressure; most other segments holding prices.
items.quote: I think by and large most segments are holding up the price. So I am hoping there should not be any negative impact except for maybe vitamin B3 where we have seen some decline in the last few weeks which may linger into Q3.

items.statement: Zettaone standalone business grew 60-70% this year; market growing 35-40% annually; semiconductor funnel increased ~30% in recent months due to joint go-to-market efforts.
items.quote: In the last few years, the business has doubled and even this year, we are hoping it will grow at least 60% 70% and possibly even more.

items.statement: Large CDMO contract future volumes under discussion with multiple scenarios; visibility expected within few weeks; take-or-pay receivable risk fully protected per agreement.
items.quote: We are very close to concluding what the way forward would be and as soon as we have the visibility, we will be able to disclose that to all of you, hopefully within next few weeks.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals EBITDA margin at 25% in Q2 driven by improved pricing in value-added fine chemicals and CDMO portfolio.
items.quote: We delivered EBITDA of INR140 crore, translating into a strong EBITDA margin of 25%, driven by improved pricing across our value-added fine chemicals and CDMO portfolio.

items.statement: Confirmed CDMO molecule pipeline at 25+ with peak revenue potential INR1,500 crore+; adding ~25 molecules per year from 100+ funnel.
items.quote: Overall, we have 25 plus confirmed molecules in our pipeline, which are expected to drive our future growth in coming years.

items.statement: Input and utility costs partially offset improved acetyls pricing; chemical intermediates saw higher input costs from elevated crude prices.
items.quote: However, input and utility costs during the quarter partially offset the benefits of improved pricing.

items.statement: Acetyls volumes stable with pharma crude prices supporting improved realization; acetic anhydride healthy sequential volume growth from resilient pharma demand and Europe market share gains.
items.quote: Acetic anhydride delivered healthy sequential volume growth supported by resilient pharma demand and market share gains in Europe while maintaining a stable domestic market position.

items.statement: Revenue from stationary engine segment for data centers to reach $100 million peak by FY30, with 30% by FY28 and 50% by FY29
items.quote: FY'30, we will reach the run rate at least by Q3 or Q4 for that $100 million. 30% by FY'28 is what we feel, 50% by FY'29.

items.statement: Committed to 15% CAGR growth in real terms on a large base
items.quote: we have committed a 15% CAGR. Of course, some years we will grow much more than that. In the real terms not adjusted for inflation is what we say that we will be growing at 15%.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA target of 1.7-1.8x on consolidated basis for the year
items.quote: overall I think we will be at 1.7-1.8 net debt to EBITDA on a consolidated basis for the year.

items.statement: Inflection point at Rs 1,850 crores EBITDA next year, after which company will be self-sufficient for capex funding
items.quote: the inflection point for us is around Rs. 1,850 crores sort of EBITDA which we wi ll reach next year. After that we will be able to be self - sufficient for funding our CAPEX as well as the maintenance CAPEX

items.statement: Q3 capex expected at Rs 500-600 crores on consolidated level; Q4 capex to be minimal as long-term projects pushed to subsequent years
items.quote: Q3 on a console level will be between Rs. 500 crores-Rs. 600 crore on the CAPEX.

items.statement: German subsidiary machine shop investment very small, around Rs 20-30 crores; no major foreign capex or acquisitions planned
items.quote: maybe 20, 30 crores on a couple of machines there, so that we can support the foundry and reduce the working capital intent.

items.statement: Alloy wheel business at around 70% utilization in past couple of months
items.quote: Sir, we are at around 70% sort of current utilization level in the past couple of months, I would say.

items.statement: DR Axion Plant-2 started trial production with strong order book; Sunbeam transformation underway with Q3/Q4 expected to be better
items.quote: The DR Axion Plant-2 has started at least trial production I would say and the order book is also strong there. Sunbeam has gone through a very good transformation and we are in close contact with the customers on the way forward. Q3 and Q4 will be looking better for Sunbeam.

items.statement: Aluminum margin decline to 6.5% EBIT margin temporary; expects recovery after price correction discussions with customers in next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, we have seen some corrections of the margins in Aluminum that is not a correction, it is a temporary correction. We had increased our inventory because of the shortage of raw material and also the prices which were increasing dropped suddenly so we had an impact of that. So, with the price increase what we are negotiating with the customer or correction or compensation for the Aluminum price

items.statement: Price rationalization needed across legacy products due to sharp rise in manpower, energy and capital goods costs; reset magnitude 6-7% to 15-20% on gross margin/value addition portion
items.quote: It may vary, but anywhere between 6% -7% all the way to 15% -20% will be there depending on the commodity, the product and the time of the order. This is not on the top line, but on the gross margin or the value addition portion.

items.statement: Sunbeam exiting low-margin businesses; top line may reduce but absolute margins will improve as some products were negative at EBITDA level
items.quote: our top line may reduce, but our absolute margins will improve because some of them are negative on the EBITDA itself in general. There's no point in trying to reset those prices. So, with that, the P&L will be very healthy.

items.statement: Stationary engine order book around $100 million for data centers; inquiries and order push for next level of capacity quite strong
items.quote: The revenues will start from FY'29 and go into FY'30 where we will peak at around $100 million and the next level of peak we are expecting in the enquiries and order push is quite strong.

items.statement: Aluminum order pipeline long for order wins; new plants ramping up with operating leverage to improve in two quarters
items.quote: On the Aluminum, the pipeline is quite long for the whatever order wins we have. There are some headwinds on the new plants where we have to put in the working capital in and we have to start up the plants which is also happening as a suboptimum as of now. So, the operating leverage on those plants will take another two quarters to get into a profitable situation.

items.statement: India becoming manufacturing hub for powertrain exports to underdeveloped markets, South America, Africa, Asia; exports of tractors, two-wheelers, construction equipment increasing
items.quote: exports out of India as a product or an aggregate will continue to grow. So, there is opportunity for all tier 1, tier 2 suppliers like craftsman for on the growth strategy.

items.statement: Aluminum price spike and drop caused inventory impact; negotiating compensation with customers for past and future corrections
items.quote: We had increased our inventory because of the shortage of raw material and also the prices which were increasing dropped suddenly so we had an impact of that. So, with the price increase what we are negotiating with the customer or correction or compensation for the Aluminum price correction also which will play out in the coming two quarters.

items.statement: Gross debt increased due to working capital ballooning from significant top-line growth, GST credit buildup, pipeline inventory, and safety stock; safety stock to dilute in coming quarter
items.quote: Our top line growth is quite significant. So, working capital has ballooned and also the other say GST credit has ballooned and some of the pipeline we have added more lines or more plants. So, that pipeline inventory is yet to materialize into revenue on the matter. So, yes, and we are also carrying some safety stock of material which now will get diluted in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Broad-basing Aluminum components beyond legacy parts; seeing opportunities in EV and wider OEM product offerings
items.quote: we are also broad basing on the new product on the Aluminum components, not only the legacy parts but I think there are more opportunities coming in not only on the EV but in general, the product offerings of the OEMs have become more wider.

items.statement: Being more selective on customers and products based on lifecycle and profitability; able to attract larger customers with more profitable products
items.quote: We are little more selective on the customers as well as the product looking at the lifecycle and profitability since we have now the base which is stronger and our ability to attract slightly larger customers with more profitable products for supply within India or outside India is better now.

items.statement: Multinational OEMs using India as export hub for aggregates; 1.5L and below gasoline powertrains and sub-150cc two-wheelers major export opportunities
items.quote: whatever can be manufactured in India is getting shifted to India and India is being used as an export hub for the aggregates also. So, 1.5 liter and below for the passenger vehicle, especially on the gasoline side, it makes a lot of sense for any OEM to get the powertrain out of India, exported out of India.

items.statement: Aluminum content per vehicle in India less than half of developed markets on ICE, maybe one-third; significant scope for growth on both ICE and EV platforms
items.quote: India has got one of the lowest Aluminum content per vehicle on the ICE also, and plus on the EV also, both. So, comparably, as a percentage of the vehicle weight on the ICE, we are less than half of the developed market, not even half, maybe one- third.

items.statement: Not a fan of investing outside India in big way due to associated risks; German subsidiary investment strategic and small; averse to foreign acquisitions
items.quote: I want to make one very clear statement is, we are not a fan of investing outside India in a big way because we understand the risks which are associated. This is a very strategic investment and we will keep it in that way.

items.statement: Commodity price risk on Aluminum; cannot get margin on increased Aluminum price; some moderation expected
items.quote: commodity price is a subject where we cannot get the increased Aluminum price, we cannot get a margin for that Aluminum also. So, we have to look at it that way. Some moderation will be there.

items.statement: CDMO revenue target of Rs 1,000 crores advanced to FY27 from FY28
items.quote: Based on the current orders of existing as well as new CDMO contracts, we now believe we will achieve this target one year ahead of schedule. It means in FY '27, we will be achieving this Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: New CDMO revenue target of Rs 2,000 crores set for FY30
items.quote: Here, I would like to say that this CDMO business will be double in next 3 financial years. It means from Rs. 1,000 crores, the new target we had set is Rs. 2,000 crore by FY 2030.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance revised from 25% to around 30% for FY27
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would also like to revise our revenue growth guidance for current year from 25% to around 30%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance raised to 38%-40% range for FY27
items.quote: We are also raising our EBITDA margin guidance between 38%-40% range for FY '27.

items.statement: New CDMO contracts expected to start contributing revenue from H2 FY27
items.quote: We are happy to share that we have received orders for new CDMO contracts which are expected to start contributing revenue from H2 FY '27.

items.statement: 8-9 CDMO products getting into revenue stream in next 1 to 1.5 years
items.quote: And there are 8-9 products in total you can say that these are getting into revenue stream in next 1 to 1-1/2 year time.

items.statement: H2 FY27 additional capex of Rs 1,650 million including Rs 1,000 million for electronic-grade chemicals and Rs 450 million for electrolyte additive phase 2
items.quote: So, in H2 FY '27, we plan to do additional CAPEX of Rs. 1,650 million CAPEX which will have around Rs. 1,000 million for electronic-grade chemicals, Rs. 450 million for second phase of electrolyte additive CAPEX and remaining will be for the maintenance CAPEX.

items.statement: Electronic-grade chemicals plant expected to start production by H1 FY29 after 1.5 year capex completion
items.quote: As we just announced the CAPEX, it will take 1-1/2 year time to get CAPEX to get completed. So maybe by H1 FY '29, we should be starting the production.

items.statement: Pharmaceutical Intermediate demand remains robust with successful cost pass-through
items.quote: Demand environment remains robust and whatever cost pressures we face due to geopolitical issues, we have been able to pass them on successfully.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin expanded 637 bps YoY to 62.1% driven by higher pharma intermediate contribution
items.quote: The gross margin expanded by 637 basis point Y-o-Y to 62.1%. Gross margin was driven by higher contribution from pharma intermediate business compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 40.3%, up 914 bps YoY driven by gross margin expansion and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margins were at 40.3% up 914 basis point Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin was driven by expansion in gross margin as well as operating leverage.

items.statement: Electrolyte additive pricing based on long-term contracts with raw material and FX pass-through, not spot prices

items.statement: Semiconductor chemicals capacity focused on Korea, Japan, Taiwan export markets; India ecosystem not yet mature

items.quote: And, planning to close the financial year at, around ₹580 Cr to ₹600 Cr as a top line, and, double the PAT margin, EBITDA say ₹12.5 Cr for H1 result.

items.statement: Top 3 with major airlines (Air India, Emirates, Qatar, Lufthansa); serve large supermarkets Lulu, Nesto via charters

items.statement: Expanding into South America trade lane; hired senior person in Brazil, inquiries materializing into business
items.quote: We have got a lot of inquiries after he's joined, and those inquiries have materialized also, business has begun also. So we want to build on that, going forward.

items.quote: Whatever our margins are, even if the Freight is double, tripled, we'll still maintain our margins. That's what we try and do as much as possible. And I can assure you, 90% of the time we do that.

items.statement: Fuel prices drive freight rates; expect fuel prices to continue current trend till end of year

items.statement: Asset-light model: all warehouses leased, no owned land or assets

items.statement: Hired senior person in Brazil to build sales team; back office team in India supporting South America expansion
items.quote: We have hired like, a small back office team in India, and we have a senior person in Brazil who will be looking at setting up a team there, and also going to be, but that team is going to be mainly sales-focused.

items.statement: India e-commerce logistics $19.54B in 2025, projected $103.83B by 2034; pharma exports >$21B in FY25

items.statement: Freight rates volatile due to geopolitical factors (war, airspace restrictions) and fuel prices

items.statement: First company to ship cargo from Navi Mumbai Airport; certified by airport and Air India
items.quote: From Navi Mumbai Airport, we were the first company to give cargo out of Navi Mumbai Airport, by the way. First, first shipment air cargo shipment that went out on Navi Airport went through us.

items.statement: Number one in perishables in India; highest volume of mangoes to US/UK, Chinese-cut roses globally
items.quote: We are currently the number one in perishables in India. We do the highest volume more than any multinational company, more than anyone, we do the highest volume out of India.

items.statement: Quarterly average AUM was INR 1.43 lakh crores, up 8% sequentially and 21% year-on-year.
items.quote: The sharpest part of market correction has came in last few weeks of October. So after the September quarter has ended. As a result, quarterly AUM of Q2 FY27 remained strong at INR1.43 lakh crores. This was up by 8% sequentially and 21% year-on-year.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 16.2% year-on-year to INR 1.37 lakh crores, driven 80% by net sales and strong SIP flows.
items.quote: Equity AUM has increased from INR1.17 lakh crores in September 2025 to INR1.37 lakh crores in September 2026. This is a growth of 16.2% or nearly INR19,100 crores. Around 80% of this growth came from net sales, supported by strong SIP flows.

items.statement: Quarterly net sales hit a record high of INR 4,137 crores despite negative mark-to-market impact of INR 1,867 crores.
items.quote: Despite a negative mark-to-market impact of INR1,867 crores, our Equity AUM grew by 1.7% sequentially. We recorded net sales of INR4,137 crores during the quarter. This is the highest quarterly net sales in our history.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book reached INR 1,272 crores, up 17.2% year-on-year; SIP market share rose to 3.73% from 3.49%.
items.quote: As of September 2026, our monthly SIP book stood at INR1,272 crores a growth of 17.2% over last one year. Our SIP collections are growing faster than the market. As a result, our share of SIP contribution has increased from 3.49% in September 2025 to 3.73% in September 2026.

items.statement: Market share in equity-oriented AUM (ex-ETF) improved to 2.7% from 2.59% a year ago.
items.quote: Our market share in equity-oriented AUM, excluding ETF, has also improved. It rose from 2.59% to 2.7% over the same period.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 11.8% sequentially; operating profit grew 15.4% with operating margin expanding 80 bps to 26.4%.
items.quote: Given the strong performance across all our businesses, our revenue from operations grew by 11.8% sequentially. Operating profit grew at a much faster pace of 15.4% sequentially on account of operating leverage and operating margin, which has been expanded by 80 basis points to 26.4%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 20% to INR 736 crores; operating profit grew 37.6% to INR 192 crores with margin at 26.1% vs 22.7% last year.

items.statement: MF yield remained stable at 88-89 bps; insurance revenue grew 35% sequentially driven by fresh premium growth of 54% in GI and 37% in life.
items.quote: MF yield otherwise has remained very, very stable between 88 to 89 basis points during the quarter. Our insurance revenue grew by a strong 35% sequentially. This was supported by fresh premium growth of 54% in general insurance and 37% in life insurance.

items.statement: Other income fell 82% sequentially to INR 3.8 crores due to mark-to-market drag on debt portfolio and reversal of hybrid portfolio gains.
items.quote: Higher bond yield created a mark-to-market drag on the debt portfolio. The hybrid portfolio also saw a reversal of earlier mark-to-market gain. As a result, other income fell by around 82% sequentially from INR20.8 crores in previous quarter to INR3.8 crores in the current quarter.

items.statement: Reported PAT declined 4.1% sequentially to INR 71.7 crores due to other income drop; operating PBT grew 16% sequentially and 45% year-on-year.
items.quote: And because of that, our reported profit after tax was at INR71.7 crores, which was down by 4.1% compared to the previous quarter. I would ask you to separate that from the operating performance because they tell a very different story. If we set aside our other income, which is treasury line and not an operating one, profit before tax grew by 16% sequentially and 45% year-on-year.

items.statement: Proposed insurance regulation differentiates IDE (Prudent) and IDA (individual agents); IDE renewal commission at 5% vs 10% for IDA in health insurance.

items.statement: Insurance business contributes ~12% of profit; if regulation implemented as drafted, impact would be significant but unlikely to remain as proposed.

items.statement: Regulator is receptive to industry representations; expects a workable middle ground to emerge on commission parity.

What industry is asking is at minimum, we should have a level playing field wit h the independent agents. We should be at par with them or somewhat higher

items.statement: Holds OBPP license; awaiting final SEBI framework for Fixed Income Channel Partner (FICP) to launch online bond business via MFD network.

They call it as FIC P. So I think consultation paper is in the process to define the FICP framework, and we are awaiting the final clarity on that before we launch it full fledged.

items.statement: Added ~3,541 new distributors in H1 FY27, ~30% higher than H1 FY26; 1,792 distributors obtained SIF certification with SIF AUM near INR 900 crores.
items.quote: This is reflected in our onboarding numbers. We added around 3,541 new distributors on our platform in the first half. That is nearly 30% higher than the first half of last year. We are also very strongly focused on scaling our SIF business. So far 1792 distributors across our MFD networks have obtained SIF certification and our SIF AUM is nearly INR900 crores.

I think because of that number, I think my provisioning on the additional trail has gone up by INR2.

items.statement: Renewal commissions to POSPs are pass-through; if IDE renewal income drops, payable commission to POSPs will reduce accordingly from April.
items.quote: Every year renewal contract. So whenever our receivable changes on the renewal side, our payable commission also changes on the renewal side. So from April onwards, assuming that our renewal commission on the health book reduces, we will be able to pass it on the reduction to the POSPs as well. Of course, the absolute margin will get impacted.

items.statement: Insurance regulation could significantly impact POSP business viability if 5% vs 10% commission differential persists; volume may not justify revenue.
items.quote: It is going to be a big, big impact for platform like Prudent or the corporate agent like Prudent in insurance POSP business. But I believe volume might increase -- but of course, that might not justify the revenue. So that is point two.

items.statement: Regulatory changes historically cause initial pain but long-term industry growth; distributors adapt by increasing volumes to offset commission cuts.
items.quote: Distributors have realized that there would be a cut in the commercial, but that is compensated by way of increasing the volume. So, unlike the entry load cut this time -- last 2 years, 3 years, I think whatever last 2 times, 3 times, whenever there was a cut in the commercial, we did not see any impact on our distribution business.

items.statement: Current AUM slightly below H1 FY27 average of INR 1.38 lakh crores due to sharp market correction in late October after quarter-end.

items.statement: Capex funded by internal accruals, bridge loan, equity if needed; negligible leverage currently
items.quote: The overall investment of INR202 crores will be funded primarily through a combination of internal accruals, bridge loan financing and equity fund raise if required.

items.statement: Hose capacity utilization currently ~80%; peak revenue potential INR850-900 crores at 70-75% utilization of 30M meter capacity

items.statement: Skid capacity utilization expected 40-50% in FY27; target peak utilization by FY28
items.quote: So yes, I think we are expecting that for this financial year, we would be reaching closer to about anywhere between 40% to 50% of our utilization of our total capacity utilization.

items.statement: Freight and forwarding costs increased significantly due to international shipping issues
items.quote: The only one concern is that the cost of the shipments have increased significantly. items.statement: Depreciation method changed from WDV to SLM effective April 1 2026, reducing depreciation by INR8.41 crores in Q2 and H1

This change resulted in a reduction in depreciation expense of INR8.41 crores, both for Q2 and for H1.

items.statement: International skid designs differ from India designs; require separate qualification, audits, controls
items.quote: No. So, I would just like to clarify that the design of SFN internationally and the design of SFN in India is different. items.statement: Granted patent for automated 3D CAD model generation for braided hose assemblies
items.quote: I'm also glad to share that we have been granted a patent for our invention of developing a system and method for automatically generating a 3D computer-aided model for braided hose assemblies.

items.statement: Vertiv largest global player in liquid cooling; market size $4-5B growing >30% YoY

items.statement: Uniware revenue growth expected >15% YoY from Q4 FY27; Shipway revenue growth expected >20% YoY from Q4 FY27
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering more than 15% year -on-year revenue growth in Un iware from Quarter 4 FY27 onwards. For Shipway, we continue to expect year-on-year revenue growth to accelerate to more than 20% from Quarter 4 FY27 onwards.

items.statement: Shipway adjusted EBITDA break-even expected Q3 FY27; PAT profitability expected Q4 FY27
items.quote: For Shipway specifically, we expect the business to achieve adjusted EBITDA profitability starting Quarter 3 FY27, followed by PAT profitability starting Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated profitability and margins expected to improve in H2 FY27 due to moderating investments and operating leverage
items.quote: Due to this, at a consolidated level, we expect profitability and margins t o improve during the second half of FY27, supported by continued revenue growth and increasing operating leverage.

items.statement: Uniware adjusted EBITDA margin at 36% in Q2 FY27; consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin at 17% in Q2 FY27

items.statement: Steady-state adjusted EBITDA margin target 20%+ as investments taper and operating leverage improves
items.quote: The idea is that steady state it should go back to 20% plus levels. As the last few quarters, we stepped up our investments in people, product, and market reach. As these investments translate into results, we anticipate increasing operating leverage, demonstrating increasing operating leverage and increasing profitability in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Uniware added 121 enterprise clients in Q2 FY27, up 17.5% YoY; onboarding 120-150 clients per quarter vs 85-90 at listing
items.quote: During Quarter 2 FY27, we added 121 enterprise clients, compared with 103 clients in the same quarter last year, representing a growth of 17.5%. These additions included both traditional enterprises and digital-first brands across multiple categories.

items.statement: UniReco and UniCapture crossed INR3 crores annualized revenue run rate (~2.5% of Uniware revenue); 150+ clients using these modules
items.quote: UniReco and UniCapture have crossed an annualized revenue run rate of over INR3 crores, representing around 2.5% of Uniware revenues. During quarter 2 FY27, more than 150 clients were using these products.

items.statement: Shipway crossed INR100 crores annualized revenue run rate; grew >15% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: With this growth, Shipway has crossed INR100 crores in annualized revenue run rate. Last three quarters, we were focused on building a strong foundation and investments to ensure sustainable growth, which is expected to be visible in the coming quarters.

items.statement: ~10% client overlap between Uniware and Shipway; 20-25% of Shipway shipment volumes from Uniware clients; cross-sell headroom significant
items.quote: Today, there is approximately 10% client overlap between Uniware and Shipway. However, almost 20% to 25% of Shipway Unicommerce e shipment volumes are already generated by clients who use Uniware. This provides significant headroom to increase cross-selling within the Uniware ecosystem

items.statement: International revenue contribution doubled to ~6% of Uniware revenue over two years; growing faster than domestic; profitable
